question: Buspirone has no cross-tolerance with benzodiazepines because it acts on 5-HT₁A receptors, not GABA-A — therefore it cannot suppress benzodiazepine withdrawal symptoms in a patient being switched from long-term BZD therapy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Because buspirone acts on 5-HT₁A receptors (not GABA-A), it cannot substitute for BZDs pharmacologically. Patients previously on BZDs often report buspirone 'doesn't work' — this is partly withdrawal anxiety (which buspirone cannot suppress) and partly the 2–4 week onset delay. Both must be explained during the transition.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Buspirone's mechanism (5-HT₁A partial agonism) is completely independent of the GABA-A receptor system. A patient transitioning from chronic BZD therapy to buspirone will not have their BZD withdrawal suppressed by buspirone — the BZD must be tapered separately while buspirone takes 2–4 weeks to reach full anxiolytic effect.
